candidates.source_body_excerpt: As fans head to the Crown Oil Arena for the first home match of the season today, police are renewing their pledge to keep supporters safe and ensuring football remains a welcoming environment for everyone. Working closely with Rochdale AFC and all Greater Manchester clubs, local authorities and partner organisations, Greater Manchester Police is continuing its intelligence-led approach to football policing, with extensive planning taking place ahead of fixtures across Greater Manchester to support public safety and prevent crime and disorder. A key part of this work is GMP’s Safeguarding at Football Events (SAFE) initiative, which aims to create a safer environment for all supporters, staff and visitors attending matches, including the thousands expected to cheer on The Dale against Crawley Town later. Building on the progress made during the 2025/26 season, officers and partners will continue to engage with fans throughout the season, raising awareness of violence against women and girls (VAWG), supporting vulnerable people and encouraging reporting of harmful behaviour. Chief Superintendent Colette Rose, Head of Specialist Operations, said: “Football should be a safe and enjoyable experience for everyone. Through our SAFE initiative, we are working closely with clubs, partners and supporters to tackle violence against women and girls, protect vulnerable people and ensure everyone feels safe attending matches. “The vast majority of supporters attend football to enjoy the game, but there is no place for abusive, threatening or discriminatory behaviour. “We will continue to take action against those who commit offences this season and work with partners to make football safer for all.” READ MORE: Green light for shopping centre’s new look

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Middleton Shopping Centre has been given permission to carry out the next phase of work to improve the look of the site. The centre, which was sold to AG Retail – a subsidiary of the Adhan Group – in June, applied to Rochdale Council to add signage to the side of the centre facing the bus station. The centre offers 324,078 sq ft of retail space across 87 units, with a 430‐space multi‐storey car park. Retailer Boyes is currently fitting out the former Wilko unit and Mother Hubbard is fitting out the corner unit close to the bus station. Planning documents submitted to the council state: “The proposal comprises the creation of two signage zones to the existing bus station car park elevation. “The zones would comprise powder-coated aluminium panels finished in grey to match the existing elevation. The works are intended to provide a coordinated, robust and visually consistent zone for future tenant signage. READ MORE: Plenty to get your teeth into when Rochdale AFC take on Crawley Town “The application should be viewed in the context of the wider programme of investment and enhancement works at Middleton Shopping Centre. Planning permission was granted on July 4, 2025, under for the introduction of eight short-stay parking bays and two disabled parking bays to the south of the shopping centre.

The visit brought together representatives from Austria's town centre management sector with local market and council leaders. During the visit, delegates toured the market's bustling trading areas, explored the surrounding retail offer, and viewed the nearby Casewell's development.

Representatives from Bury Council and industry bodies, including Market Service Manager Simon Green, Councillor Gavin McGill, and the CEO of NABMA David Catterall, shared insights into the market's award-winning success, the town centre masterplan, and the council's long-standing support for the market as a key driver of economic growth and community life.

The delegation specifically requested a visit to Bury as part of work on the Danube Culinarium Tulln project. Located on the banks of the River Danube, Tulln is developing a new market facility and was keen to learn how Bury has built and maintained a thriving market destination, overcome challenges and planned for future growth.

Roland Murauer, Chief Executive Officer of CIMA (Austria City Centre Management), said:

"England's pioneering role in the field of town centre and high street development, already well known on the continent, was impressively reaffirmed during this professional study tour to Bury.

“In particular, the long-term strategic and operational cooperation between the various stakeholder groups and local government offers valuable insights for us in Austria.

“During this study tour of market halls in England, we gained many interesting insights in Bury for our planned Danube Culinarium Tulln project in Austria. We were particularly impressed by how well Bury Market is integrated into the commercial zones, as well as the clear boost it provides to the town centre's economic prosperity.

The adjoining Caswell's development will add a huge boost to the town centre when it opens later in the year."

Ged Gibbons MSc, who accompanied the delegation, said:

"The warmth of our reception in Bury was recognised by our friends from Austria. It is clear that Bury has true professionals delivering quality markets, with great product knowledge and first-class operational delivery."

Councillor Gavin McGill, Cabinet Member for Culture, Economy and Skills, said: "In Bury we are rightly proud to call our market world-famous.

"That's why I was very pleased to welcome the delegation from Austria, alongside the market team and industry bodies.

"Talking about Bury's progress through investment in the new market canopy and Casewells, as well as other projects in Bury centre and the wider town, tells the world that Bury is the place to be.

"I look forward to welcoming more such delegations and customers to Bury Market in the future."

The visitors also met market traders, who provided a traditional Bury welcome and showcased local produce, helping demonstrate the unique character and appeal that continues to attract shoppers and visitors from across the region and beyond.

Bury Market is widely recognised as one of the country's leading markets and continues to play a central role in supporting local businesses, attracting visitors and contributing to the ongoing regeneration of Bury town centre.
candidates.source_summary: A senior delegation from Austria has visited Bury Market to learn more about the success of one of the UK's most celebrated markets and its role in supporting the wider town centre economy.

Market Street now has improved access for communities in Fishpool and Pimhole, making it easier to reach local shops, services, public transport, and the town centre by walking and cycling, while reducing reliance on short car journeys.

The scheme included work to Market Street:

  • Two new pedestrian-controlled crossings
  • Two upgraded bus stops
  • One new continuous footpath at the entrance to Bury Athletics Club
  • Separated cycle and pedestrian route from traffic with the shared space widened along the full length of Market Street.
  • One new raised table at the junction with Trinity Street
  • Resurfacing of the whole road from junction with Angouleme Way to 50m south of the junction with Wellington Road.

On Wellington Road:

  • The roundabout was replaced with a CYCLOPS junction which separates cyclists and pedestrians from other traffic
  • Resurfacing of Wellington Road from its junction with Grosvenor Street to the entrance of Grundy Hub field.

The improvements complement recent upgrades at the junction of Market Street and Angouleme Way, at Gigg Lane, and the work taking place at the junction of Parkhills Road and Manchester Road.

Councillor Lucy Smith Cabinet Member for Environment, Climate Change, and Operations said: “I’d like to thank everyone for their patience while these key improvement works have been carried out.

“These changes should make it easier and safer for people to walk, cycle or use mobility aids for everyday trips, such as going to school, work, or the shops.

“Thank you for everybody’s patience while these works were done, particularly for people travelling along Manchester Road while we improve the junction with Parkhills Road.

“The work has been timed for the school holidays to minimise disruption, and once the new signals are in place we will carry out the resurfacing work at night.”

The £5.7m Fishpool and Pimhole Active Travel Scheme forms part of the Bee Network and is funded through the UK Government’s City Region Sustainable Transport Settlement (CRSTS) and the Mayor of Greater Manchester’s Challenge Fund.

Work is ongoing at the junction of Parkhills Road and Manchester Road improving the junction and installing new traffic crossing signals.

Once this work is finished Manchester Road will be resurfaced between Gigg Lane and Ashlor Street with night closures and signed diversions. This work is expected to start during the early part of September.

Hekmat Omar Ali Hakim, an Iraqi national of St. James Road, Higher Broughton, has been charged with failing to disclose information regarding terrorist activity under Section 38b of the Terrorism Act 2000.

Hakim, whose self-defined ethnicity is Asian, has been remanded to appear before Westminster Magistrates Court today.

The charge relates directly to the antisemetic terrorist attack which took place on the morning of Thursday 2 October 2025, during the holiest day of the Jewish calendar, Yom Kippur, where three were killed, including the attacker, Jihad Al-Shamie, and three more were injured.

Melvin Cravitz and Adrian Daulby were sadly killed. All of the three who were injured have since been released from hospital.

Assistant Chief Constable Rob Potts, who holds operational responsibility for Counter Terrorism Policing North West, said: “I can confirm that, earlier today, officers from Counter Terrorism Policing North West charged a man with failing to disclose information regarding terrorist activity. This charge is directly related to the terrorist attack which took place at the Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation Synagogue last October.

“This is a significant development in our investigation, and my thoughts are with all those affected by the attack, particularly the bereaved loved ones and survivors. We have updated them and continue to offer them as much support as possible.

“Since the attack took place, we have been unwavering in our commitment to establishing the full picture behind the incident and identifying anybody who may have been involved in any way.

“The charge that has been authorised is the culmination of a substantial amount of meticulous work by the investigation team, supported by the Crown Prosecution Service, and I hope this update reaffirms that commitment.”

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale will have a chance to remember legendary comedian Jimmy Cricket ahead of his funeral next week. Jimmy died on August 3, aged 80, after a short illness with his family around him. Known for his clean humour, the Northern Ireland comedian became a household name in the 1970s after working the comedy club scene. Famous for his catchphrase “And there’s more”, he lived in Rochdale and was a big supporter of local charities and causes. On Thursday, August 20, his body will lie in state at St Patrick’s Catholic Church in Rochdale from 3pm to 5pm on for anyone wanting to pay their respects. His life will then be celebrated at Salford Cathedral starting with a vigil mass for the reception of the body at 7pm. It will be followed by his funeral at 1.30pm on Friday, August 21, at the cathedral, with mourners encouraged to wear bow ties which, along with his Wellington boots, became Jimmy’s trademark. candidates.source_body_excerpt: A deli in Rochdale was broken into but thieves only got away with a can of Fanta and a pack of cigarettes. Rachel Ward only opened the Healey Deli, on Market Street in Whitworth , back in October, but in a short space of time it has managed to build up a reputation for its sandwiches, breakfasts, drinks, and ice cream sundaes. In the early hours of Tuesday morning (August 18), Rachel claimed the shop door was broken into, with thieves smashing a window and using a crowbar to break into a till. But, posting on social media, Rachel said that the incident could have been much worse. Click here for the latest on Manchester's food & drink scene, gigs and more in our CityLife newsletter The cafe owner posted: “WELL… HEALEY DELI HAS OFFICIALLY MADE THE BIG TIME! Unfortunately, we had some unwanted visitors who decided to break into Healey Deli. “After smashing their way in, our criminal masterminds made off with… An emergency packet of cigarettes from the till and ONE Fanta Fruit Twist. That’s it. Not the food, not the coffee, not even the Spam. Apparently the getaway plan required a quick fag and a tropical fizzy drink.” In response to the post, some customers also took the opportunity to make light of the situation. One person posted: "What time do you open in the morning, knowing the spam is safe will pop in for a spam butty." Another said: "Awww Rach, really what was the point, all that damage and they didn't even kidnap the spam!" Despite seeing the funny side of the incident, Rachel told the Manchester Evening News that she was upset over the distress caused by the break-in and the damage that has been caused. She explained: "It is a shame that things like this happen. It is quite hurtful when someone comes in and damages your business that you’ve worked so hard on, especially all for pretty much nothing. We work hard, so it’s very frustrating. “We had to close the business for a day, we’re having to pay to get things repaired. It costs time and money to get these things all fixed and get back on track. It's just something we could have done without. “But I am also aware that there are worse things going on in the world. It’s one of those things where it’s just a case of having to move on from it - the show still goes on. “It has shown me how much of a real community spirit there is in the local neighbourhood. So many people have reached out to me to ask me if they can help me get my door fixed, or get security systems installed. It’s been very humbling.” Lancashire Police confirmed they had received a report of the incident, and are investigating the matter.
candidates.source_summary: They didn't get away with much

A colossal scheme to build 1,550 homes has been earmarked for green fields just off the M60.

The villages of Simister and Bowlee offer a rural lifestyle for local residents, surprisingly located next to one of the north west’s busiest motorway junctions – Simister Island. Sat right on the Bury/Rochdale border, the 98 hectares of farmland will effectively be transformed into a new village.

A new ‘local centre’, a primary school, bus routes, cycle ways and footpaths have all been touted for the project. The site would be delivered over several years and split into three parts – north, south and east, bisected by Heywood Old Road (the A6045). 

The southern parcel is expected to deliver around 800 homes, with 550 in the north and 200 in the east.

The ‘countryside beauty’ would be maintained throughout the site, according to the development framework, with green spaces and ‘pocket parks’ lining the walking and cycling routes throughout. 

The development framework claims this ‘active travel’ network would stretch as far as Heaton Park and link the site to surrounding towns and villages such as Simister next door, Middleton and Prestwich. Transport links to the impending Atom Valley development zone is also on the cards – offering connection to the estimated 20,000 new jobs.

Thousands more homes and the creation of vast amounts of industrial/work space is part of the major overhaul in the north eastern section of Greater Manchester. In Bury, Elton Reservoir is set to gain 3,500 new homes, with a further 1,250 planned for Walshaw. 

Including Simister Bowlee, this would total 6,300 new homes around the area. With this in mind, new transport links are seen as key to connecting the new homes to what is expected to become the largest and most accessible employment and innovation hubs in the region, driving substantial investment into Greater Manchester.

Forgotten areas on the edge of Rochdale are set for a makeover thanks to almost £20m in government cash.

The council are set to accept the Pride in Place funding next week at the latest town hall meeting. This means the local authority would get the total £19.6m over the course of the next decade. 

It works out at just under £2m every year for 10 years. The targeted areas are Hurstead, Smallbridge and Belfield – all of which have been overlooked for funding historically.

Currently no plan has been created to decide on how the cash will be spent. However, tackling congestion; improving parking; creating new green spaces; enhancing local facilities; and expanding maternity services are all early suggestions being made.

At their meeting next week, town hall bosses are also set to approve the Hurstead, Smallbridge and Belfield Neighbourhood Board – who will establish the proposal on how to spend the money.

The Neighbourhood Board is made up of local community figures; MP Paul Waugh; the council’s regeneration boss Coun Daniel Meredith; and chaired by Laura Rodwell of the M6 Theatre group.

According to council documents, they have until November 30, 2026 to submit their four-year plan to the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government.

This plan is necessary in order to unlock the funding. Some £150,000 has already been granted by the government in order to form the board and generate the plan.

When the Pride in Place funding was announced last year, there was understandable skepticism locally. This was due to the areas going years without proper investment. 

Ken Whittle has lived and worked in the area for decades. He felt very little investment has left the area looking tired and unloved.

Speaking previously, Ken said: “I’m very skeptical about this. People here are used to getting nothing.

“Something for the children will be good or a centre for the community to gather could work because, at the moment, that doesn’t exist.

“Social housing needs work so people can actually come in and have a home. We can’t let it go downhill any further.

“The hardest thing with this is that people are moving out because no one is doing anything with anything. There has been no investment really.

“Maybe this cash can change things, but it’s up to the community to do it properly.”

Another skeptic, Dinah Banks, told the Local Democracy Reporting Service: “I think people just get on with their own lives. Why bother, look at it, it’s got no life at the moment.

“I want to see better GP service and walk-in surgeries and not have to travel so far to get there.

“Maybe a proper community health service. But I won’t hold my breath.”

Rochdale MP Paul Waugh has already held consultation events with locals to get an understanding of what they want. 

Once the new Neighbourhood Board and government cash is formally accepted by Rochdale council’s cabinet on August 25, local views will shape how the future scheme looks.

Regent Mill is an industrial complex rather than the typical historic cotton mill you see dominating the skylines of Rochdalian towns. But the bulldozing of this deteriorating building on St James Street could unlock a wider vision for Heywood.

Rochdale council, who are carrying out the demolition work, say they hope to bring forward plans to build around 200 new homes in this area of the town. 

These homes are expected to be more affordable homes. No timeline for when this could happen has been set out.

Once the former tile merchant has been levelled, it would facilitate housing schemes to come forward, according to the local authority. This would link into Heywood’s ongoing regeneration. 

A fresh new Heywood Civic has already been completed. This has been accompanied by the makeover to Peine Square on the Civic’s doorstep.

Some £20m of the government’s Pride in Place funding is currently being spent, with grant applications for local businesses expected to be open soon. This would bring further cash directly to local organisations to better the area.

Coun Danny Meredith, cabinet member for regeneration and housing at Rochdale Borough Council, said: “The demolition of Regent Mill is part of the wider regeneration of this part of Heywood, as part of our masterplan. This will see us work with partners to transform brownfield sites around the town centre into new, high-quality much needed social homes for local people.

“Over time, we hope to bring forward more than 200 homes on and around the Regent Mill area. So where we now have empty sites, which are not visually appealing, we will have fantastic new homes to help address our housing shortage and give the whole area a lift. 

“We have already seen considerable regeneration within Heywood town centre and this project will continue this redevelopment and further support local families.”

There are some concerns about the demolition work raised by highways teams. Highways explained that recent demolitions of properties in this area ‘have caused damage to highways surfaces causing significant risk to pedestrians’.

Planning papers described how the council intends to fence off the demolition site, including debris netting and site signage to protect pedestrians and the roads.

The former chair for Heywood's Pride in Place scheme, Brian Davies, has stepped down, leaving the scheme temporarily without a chair for the £20 million initiative.

Elsie Blundell, MP for Heywood and Middleton North commented, saying: “Brian has done a fantastic job of getting the investment plan approved by government and starting the Pride in Place scheme.  Now it has to change to a delivery phase and it is exciting that we are looking for a new chair and two new board members to strengthen the board for this next important stage.

“We know that the community wants to see Pride in Place focus on three things: crime and anti-social behaviour, transport links, and facilities for young people. That’s what local residents have told us. Now we must deliver a transformation of the town, using this money.”

The Pride in Place project is led by the local community, with board members who represent different corners of Heywood's residents, community organisations, civil society, and businesses. After producing an investment plan and securing funding from the Government, the board is entering the project delivery phase, bringing forward and developing proposals for the £20m (£2m a year, for 10 years).

Elsie added:  “This is national money which can only be spent locally, led by the community.  It means an exciting new chapter in Heywood’s future to transform the town we see around us and create new opportunities for the people who live here.”

Heywood’s Pride in Place Board are looking for a new chair to lead the board through the next stage of its work, developing, and funding projects to shape the future of the town. They are also looking for two new members to join the board.

The Chair will lead engagement and keep Pride in Place focused on delivery through relationships with key stakeholder such as the Council, Rochdale Development Agency, the NHS, Action Together, and others.  Working with board members they will be responsible for sharing information, gaining consensus, and participation from the board and the community.

Elsie has said that anyone who is interested in applying can reach out to her office for a chat by emailing her. Elsie has said “We want a strong leader who is confidently about Heywood’s future, there is so much potential here.”

The deadline is 7th September.

The Greater Manchester Combined Authority is to receive £16,955,174 over three years in an attempt to tackle rough sleeping in the area as part of Prime Minister Andy Burnham's national drive to end rough sleeping that totals £442 million across the country over three years, and £37 million in the North West.

The money is to create new accommodation and support that is to be rolled out across England this winter.

Alongside emergency accommodation for those who are rough sleepers, the programme will offer help with housing, health, and other needs, in an attempt to help people build a more stable future, rather than just giving people a temporary place to stay.

Accompanying this initiative, Burnham has announced that he will host a national summit in the Autumn to bring together leaders from business, finance, charities, health, faith communities, and more to ask what role each of them could play in ending rough sleeping.

Crisis, a charity for people who are homeless, suggest that preventing 40,000 people from becoming homeless could save the taxpayer close to £370 million.

PM Andy Burnham has said:  “No-one should have to bed down in a doorway or outside a station. But we’ve seen it for so long that it feels like Westminster has started to accept it.

"I won’t accept it. That’s why my first instruction as Prime Minister was to end rough sleeping. And it’s why today we’re getting started with a national drive to get everyone in for Christmas.

"We did it in the pandemic. We can do it again. But it needs all of us. Government will put the money in. But I’m asking leaders in communities and sectors across society to play their part locally too.

"Let’s get people out the cold. And let’s bring back hope."

Of the money in the initiative, £8.4 million of the new funding is going specifically to the Ending Homelessness in Communities Fund. This takes total funding allocations announced for 100 different projects to £47 million over three years.

As well as off the street provision, the funding will help local areas deliver more than 1000 settled homes over the next three years, alongside further wraparound support to help people rebuild their lives. Labour say that areas facing the greatest pressures will receive the largest share of support, with communities all across England getting support to address rough sleeping in their area.

Alongside funding allocations, the Government is publishing guidance to help local areas mobilise quickly and deliver a consistent route off the street offer this winter. The guidance will make clear the need to ensure adequate and accessible provision for women experiencing rough sleeping, recognising that women are often underrepresented in official statistics and may be at greater risk of violence, abuse, and exploitation. Guidance encourages local areas to consider single sex accommodation with specialist, intensive and trauma informed support, for victims of domestic abuse and sexual violence. This will support the government’s commitment to halve violence against women and girls in the next ten years.

This funding comes after Andy Burnham gave his first instruction to end rough sleeping across the country.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: One of the borough's leading sports clubs joins forces with the town's professional football team to widen access to physical activity Rochdale AFC, Rochdale AFC Community Trust and Rochdale Netball Club are delighted to announce the launch of Rochdale AFC Netball. The agreement will see Rochdale Netball Club rebrand and become part of the club's wider 'Our Teams' family. The partnership brings together one of the borough's leading community sports clubs with its professional football club and official charitable arm, creating a stronger platform to grow netball and widen access to physical activity across Rochdale — from primary school participation through to junior and adult club netball, coaching, volunteering and leadership. Netball is one of the most widely played team sports in England, particularly among women and girls, with accessible formats for all ages and abilities, including junior netball, Back to Netball and Walking Netball. Under the new Rochdale AFC Netball identity, the partnership will raise the sport's profile locally, strengthen school-to-club links, and give more people a clear route into the game. Currently, Rochdale Netball Club runs teams from under-sixes right through to seniors, with nearly 200 players taking to the court every week. The agreement will also support wider community outcomes, with Rochdale AFC Community Trust working alongside Rochdale AFC Netball on new programmes in schools, holiday provision, health and wellbeing, and volunteer development. Operating under a shared Rochdale AFC identity opens up new opportunities too, from commercial support and matchday promotion to community events and sponsorship, reinforcing that women's sport has a central place in the borough's sporting future. The move follows a model seen elsewhere in professional sport, where football and rugby clubs have partnered with netball organisations to boost visibility, participation and long-term sustainability. In Rochdale, the priority will be a community-first approach that reflects the town's sporting pride and welcomes people of all ages.
